relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a boy with a heterozygous TNFAIP3 frameshift variant and an HA20 diagnosis: 'This case expands the clinical spectrum of A20 haploinsufficiency.'
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script in scratch, all values typed from reading, spans checked verbatim by script. One in-scope person, labelled 'patient' (rule 5; the paper has no own label; figure 1D calls him 'patient (P)'). Relatives not given rows: the 'healthy non-consanguineous British parents', the 'healthy unaffected siblings' and the first-born infant who 'died as a result of prematurity' (figure 1A legend) are not described as tested or affected. Table 1 has timepoint columns (Pretransplant | Post-transplant | Reference range) for the single patient; spans quote the row from its label; lab values were not turned into features unless the text names the feature (e.g. no anaemia, neutropenia or B-cell rows). Variant notation differs within the paper: text 'c.1466_1467delTG' / 'p.V489Afs*7', figure 1 legend 'c.1466_1467TGdel' / 'V489Afs*7'; the text form is recorded. The authors call the variant 'de novo' but do not describe parental testing, so inheritance is 'not reported' under rule 8; the claim is recorded in parental_testing_statement. Pathogenic variants in STAT3 and FOXP3 were 'excluded' (no variant rows). Reference 9's HA20 cohort is mentioned only at group level (no rows). The paper does not mention any earlier report of this patient, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null. Checklist: 'hepatitis', 'cytopaenias' and 'enteropathy' are marked observed for autoimmune hepatitis, cytopenia (autoimmune) and gastrointestinal inflammation because the paper presents them as features of his 'complex autoimmunity'. Age 14 is the age given at presentation of the case; the latest timepoint (21 months post-transplant) has no stated age. No internal contradictions found apart from the notation difference.

span: The clinical course was refractory to intensive immunosuppression with prednisolone, sirolimus, tacrolimus, infliximab or rituximab, necessitating haematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
Peripheral neutrophils were supported pretransplant by recombinant granulocyte colony stimulating factor.
Post-HSCT antibody indices were measured during concomitant subcutaneous immunoglobulin supplementation.
Twenty-one months post-transplant, he is thriving off all immunosuppressive medication with complete remission of autoimmune disease (except diabetes).

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: Genetic: whole exome sequencing with bioinformatic filtering identified a single plausible TNFAIP3 variant, confirmed by capillary (Sanger) sequencing, with functional studies in fibroblasts; STAT3 and FOXP3 pathogenic variants excluded
span: By whole exome sequencing of peripheral blood genomic DNA (Illumina MiSeq) and downstream bioinformatic filtering (Ingenuity Variant Analysis), we identified a single biologically plausible variant
The c.1466_1467delTG variant—which we confirmed by capillary sequencing10 (figure 1B)
Pathogenic variants in STAT3 and FOXP3 were excluded.
we performed functional experiments in patient and control dermal fibroblasts

functional_evidence_statement.value: Patient dermal fibroblasts: reduced basal and TNF-induced A20 protein (immunoblot); exaggerated and prolonged NF-kB pathway phosphorylation after TNF-alpha; global increase in TNF-alpha-stimulated differential gene expression (RNA-seq); enhanced IL-6 protein (ELISA, p=0.0015); inflammasome activation not tested for lack of leucocyte material
span: Immunoblotting10 of patient and control dermal fibroblast lysates with an N-terminal antibody confirmed the reduced basal and TNF-α-induced expression of A20 (figure 1D).
We observed exaggerated and prolonged phosphorylation of components of the NF-κB pathway
RNA sequencing (Illumina NextSeq-500) revealed a significant global increase in both the range and magnitude of TNF-α-stimulated differential gene expression
We also confirmed enhanced expression of the key NF-κB target gene interleukin 6 (IL-6) at the protein level by ELISA (p=0.0015, figure 1G).
owing to the lack of leucocyte material, we were not able to extend our analysis to inflammasome activation
a heterozygous loss-of-function mutation in TNFAIP3 (A20)
a novel de novo heterozygous 2 bp deletion
